about.title: Culver City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Culver City's mix of local traffic and freeway commuters converges at spots like Washington Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and the I-405 interchange, where public records show 80 injury collisions and 113 injured people in the most recent year, with Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. seeing more reported crashes than other times. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: California gives you two years to file a claim in most car accident cases, but insurers move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memory can fade fast. We're a personal injury team ready to review the facts, deal with the insurance company, and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and no cost unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but that window shrinks dramatically if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. We can help identify deadlines early so you don't lose your right to recover.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage of blame assigned to you reduces your compensation but doesn't bar it entirely. Insurers often try to inflate your share of fault, so having someone review the evidence on your behalf matters.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident claims. We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out what your claim may be worth.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on a city street near a Culver City intersection controlled by a traffic signal owned by the city or county?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads or signals can carry a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes as little as six months instead of two years. Because Washington Boulevard and other Culver City corridors involve various jurisdictions, it's worth having us check who's responsible for the road quickly. Missing a government claim deadline can permanently bar your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Consultations come at no cost to you. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
